subject: Post-call: parity qualification matrix, recommended models, and next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@ledgertech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: parity qualification matrix, recommended models, and next steps

Hi Anna — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap + recommended next steps for the evaluation (high level first, details attached):

Summary of discovery
- Primary goal: replace current proprietary summarization baseline for customer support tickets and preserve legal/compliance consistency.
- Key constraints: latency budget ~300ms p95 per request, throughput ~200 reqs/min for peak ingestion, strong hallucination guardrails for PII removal, and exportable audit logs.
- Acceptance: LedgerTech wants parity on quality vs baseline with measurable thresholds (see acceptance matrix below).

Recommended models to trial
- open-xxl-70b (quantized q4f): best cost/quality tradeoff for extractive QA and structured summarization.
- redwood-curated-medium (rw-medium-v1): lower-latency fallback for tail requests to keep p95 under budget.
- proprietary-baseline-v2: your current internal model (we'll use as ground truth for parity).

Acceptance/Parity matrix (proposed)
- Intent accuracy (support classification): >= 0.88 F1 compared to baseline.
- Summarization alignment (ROUGE-L / human preference): mean human pairwise pref >= 0.55 vs baseline on a seeded eval set.
- Safety/hallucination (regression): false-positive PII omissions <= 0.5% on test prompts.
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for redwood-curated-medium in canary config; open-xxl can run at p95 <= 550ms (acceptable as async heavier model).

Attached for your team
- evaluation_plan.xlsx (evaluation schedule, dataset split, acceptance gates)
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (seed prompts + negative controls)
- parity_benchmark_results.csv (initial smoke runs on synthetic set)

Quick asks / next steps
1) Please confirm the eval subset we should use as the official acceptance set. I proposed a stratified 2k-ticket sample (500 high-priority, 1.5k mixed historical); confirm or propose changes.
2) Do you require a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for the canary? We can run hosted canary for initial runs, then mirror to Private if needed.
3) Would you like Redwood to run the first pass evaluation and produce a short report (2–3 pages) we can share with your legal/compliance team?
4) Tech deep dive: suggested slots next week — Tue 12/1 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 12/2 14:00–14:30 PT.

If that all looks good I’ll loop Markus and Rachel to confirm commercial and SOW items. Thanks again — enjoyed the deep product fit discussion.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
T: +1 (415) 555-0172

--
attachments: evaluation_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (jsonl), parity_benchmark_results.csv (csv)
From: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@ledgertech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: LedgerTech Security <security@ledgertech.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: parity qualification matrix, recommended models, and next steps

Thanks Monica — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the acceptance set:

- Dataset subset: the 2k stratified sample sounds reasonable. Can we reserve ~200 tickets that touch regulatory/legal categories as a separate holdout for security review? Security team (cc’d) wants to run their own checks on hallucination risk.

- Latency: the suggested p95 buckets make sense, but is there an SLA-backed option to prioritize p95 < 300ms for the primary route if we commit to dedicated capacity? We’d like to understand the incremental cost to guarantee p95 300ms for open-xxl if we move to Dedicated.

- Canary/private deployment: security prefers us to do initial runs in a dedicated VPC (private deployment) rather than public hosted runs — can Redwood support a VPC-first canary for an initial 2-week trial? If so, what’s the onboarding timeline?

- Acceptance gates: for human pairwise pref you suggest 0.55. Our product leads typically want >= 0.6 to consider replacing proprietary baselines because of user-facing regression risk. Can you show sensitivity analyses (how many human labels needed to detect delta with 95% power) — if we need more label budget we’ll plan accordingly.

We’re keen to move to a short evaluation window — tech deep dive on Tue 12/1 10:00 PT works for us.

Regards,
Anna Jensen
Director of Product, LedgerTech
anna.jensen@ledgertech.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@ledgertech.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: parity qualification matrix, recommended models, and next steps

Anna / Monica — quick internal note and commercial readout.

- Commercial: we can offer a 60-day dedicated VPC canary for LedgerTech with limited reserved capacity (up to 4x the peak burst) and a short-term discount tied to a 6-month committed minimum. I’ll have Sales Ops send draft numbers after the tech sync.

- Latency guarantee: Dedicated pools can be configured to meet p95 <= 300ms for rw-medium-v1 at the proposed throughput. For open-xxl-70b we recommend asynchronous routing with a low-latency fallback (rw-medium) so user-facing p95 stays within the 300ms budget.

- Acceptance thresholds: I agree to Anna’s ask — bump human preference target to 0.6 as the primary gate. Monica / Dev, please include a sensitivity table in the evaluation_plan.xlsx that shows required label counts for 0.6 at 80/90/95% power so LedgerTech can budget labeling.

- Legal/SOW: Rachel — can you open an SOW draft tied to LDG-202611-058 and include a 2-week private onboarding milestone + optional extension for production rollout?

Markus
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@ledgertech.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: parity qualification matrix, recommended models, and next steps

Anna — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming next steps and logistics after Markus’ notes:

1) Evaluation set: we will hold out 200 regulatory/legal tickets as a security holdout. LedgerTech security (cc’d) will receive a sanitized subset and the hallucination checks.
2) Canary: we’ll provision a 60-day VPC canary with reserved capacity. Dev will outline the onboarding checklist during the tech deep dive.
3) Acceptance gates: update the human pairwise pref target to >= 0.6; Monica/Dev will add the sensitivity/label-budget table to the plan.
4) Commercial/SOW: Markus & Rachel will own SOW/discount language; Monica will own the evaluation report and the parity dashboard.

Tech deep dive: Tue 12/1 10:00–10:30 PT (calendar invite incoming). Please review the attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl before the call — we’ll walk through seed prompts and negative-control injections.

Deliverables timeline
- Draft evaluation runs & initial smoke report: by EOD Fri 12/4
- Sensitivity/label-budget table: by Mon 12/7
- SOW draft (initial): by Mon 12/7

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
